prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

entry.note: one pin must pass boss and both lugs: the bores share the hinge axis
at full open the lid stands clear of the wire channel for access; at zero the plate edge sits 2 mm from the rib, so this holds only AT the pose
closed flat (0 deg, as built) to full open (110 deg) - KINEMATICS.md §1 declared travel
the full-open limit configuration the pose-bound access constraint evaluates at
the plate's front-bottom edge sweeps closest to the rib just off the deck (about 4-5 deg), not at either travel end: a sampled fact only a sweep can state

notes: Difficulty 3. Corpus v3 (2026-08-27, KINEMATICS.md §6 Stage 9C): the hinge mechanism task - travel limits and a swept clearance as declared, engine-graded motion state. The task owns the joint (0..110 deg travel), the pose, the sweep and both constraints, installed over whatever the run declared, exactly as constraint acceptance already works. The numbers are hand-derived from the interface geometry: the lid's governing point is the plate's front-bottom corner edge (radius sqrt(38^2 + 7^2) = 38.639 mm about the hinge axis), the rib's governing point its near top corner (radius sqrt(40^2 + 4^2) = 40.200 mm), so the swing clearance bottoms out at 40.200 - 38.639 = 1.560 mm at ~4.7 deg - just off the deck, interior to the travel, which is why it is a sweep_clearance (bar 1.2 mm; the 56-sample grid's worst sample measures ~1.60 mm) and not a pose fact. At p-open the nearest lid geometry is the strap root's bottom edge (y = 0, z = 8: radius 7.0 mm, straight above the axis at 110 deg), 34.03 mm from the rib corner (c-open-access bar 30 mm); at zero the plate edge sits 2.0 mm from the rib, so the pose binding is load-bearing - unbound, c-open-access would be violated. CHECKS keep the single-part facts (envelopes, rest-without-bite, sealed topology: base genus 1, lid genus 2 through both lugs).
